neighbours.label: the second piece of a compound or rare name (Play|girl, Bath|gate, Lol|ita, Bal|och), not a name that is one token
fire: A cottage near Highgate was left to her by an aunt.
The old fish market at Billingsgate moved east in 1982.
We went to see the musical Evita with my parents.
A newsagent in the village stocked an old copy of Playgirl.
Tribal leaders from the Balochi region met at the border.
The classic novel Lolita caused a scandal when it appeared.
A nomad from the Baluch people led us across the desert.
Our train stopped in Bathgate for almost an hour.
quiet: A cottage near Oxford was left to her by an aunt.
The old fish market at Glasgow moved east in 1982.
We went to see the musical Hamilton with my parents.
A newsagent in the village stocked an old copy of Playboy.
Tribal leaders from the Kurdish region met at the border.
The classic novel Dracula caused a scandal when it appeared.
A nomad from the Bedouin people led us across the desert.
Our train stopped in Edinburgh for almost an hour.

notes: Card: 'ita' x2, 'ney' x2, 'uch' x2, 'och', 'girl', '-Based', 'Art' after Play, 'gate' after Bath. Probe: 'och' 0.789; Playgirl 0.703; Bathgate 0.549; Lolita 0.465; ' Med' 0.357. Near misses are one-token names in the same position. This pole overlaps in kind with L6/N8207+ and L6/N10410+.
